EXTRA CLASS · THE TODDLER ROOM

Welcome to the Toddler Room.

The room a one- to three-year-old already lives in, card by card: play time, mealtimes, the sleep corner, the care routines, getting dressed and the furniture that holds it together — every tile below opens its own step-by-step lesson, and every card page has a download button and an age pill.

HOW THIS ROOM WORKS

Thirty-five words, one room, no schedule.

The Toddler Room is a bonus class, kept deliberately beside the main learning path: the regular classes stay the core sequence, and this room is here whenever a one- to three-year-old wants more. Every card names something the child already touches every day — the ball, the crib, the sippy cup, the teddy — and every tile below opens its own step-by-step lesson: the word, the routine it lives in, the parent script and one small game.

The room is laid out the way toddlers live: play time first, then mealtimes, the sleep corner, the care routines, getting dressed, and the furniture that holds it all together. Every card carries an age pill — Ages 1+ for first words, Ages 2–3 for routines and pretend play — so you can start where your child is today and let the set grow with them. Dip in any order, in any mood, for two minutes at a time. Skipping this room leaves nobody behind; that is what a bonus is for.

LEARN WITH FLASHCARDS

Learn the toddler room, word by word.

Thirty-five cards, one picture each. Tap any picture and it opens its own lesson page — the original artwork on the left, and the step-by-step teaching on the right: what the word is, where the routine lives and the game to play tonight.

SUPPORTING RESOURCE

Print the toddler room cards.

Every lesson has a matching flashcard in the library: the original artwork as a printable card with a download button, print size and short notes for grown-ups. The same shelf keeps the first-words cards and the first concepts from the core path, if you want the toddler years in one basket.
